issues.description: The attend(course:) method signature is inconsistent between the problem statement/template and the solution. The problem description (and the template) define attend(course: Course?) with a single parameter, but the solution's Developer.swift defines attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool) with an extra Boolean parameter. Additionally, the solution's Client.swift calls myself.attend(course: swiftCourse) using the single-parameter form, which is incompatible with the solution's two-parameter implementation and would cause compilation errors. This mismatch will confuse students mapping the task to the implementation and prevents the solution from compiling as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attend method signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution's method to match the spec and template: 'func attend(course: Course?) { ... }' and implement the described behavior (optional binding, increment monthsOfSwiftExperience, print message), or (B) if the extra parameter is required, update the problem statement and template to include the second parameter and provide a default value so existing call sites remain valid (e.g. 'func attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool = true)'). The recommended fix is option (A) to align the solution with the exercise specification.
